First listed 2025-05-19 · episode or wrap

Spanning the Gamut of Financial Services with Dwight Collins

Eisman and Dwight Collins compare banking, wealth management, alternatives, insurers and payments. Collins favors durable quality and anticipates Wells Fargo regulatory relief, which arrived in June. Eisman distinguishes trading earnings from investment-banking rerating and emphasizes network economics. His categorical statements about private-equity marks, index ownership and Upstart costs need correction. Many valuations, client observations and causal investment theses remain unresolved rather than being graded from price direction alone.

YouTube · 2025-05-19 ↗
The strongest near-term validated forecast belongs to Collins: imminent Wells Fargo asset-cap removal. Eisman correctly highlights governance and accounting as important, but his private-equity accounting explanation is materially wrong. Guest recommendations remain separate from his own scorecard.

Source version, speaker attribution and transcript cautions

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

YouTube automatic captions; speaker attribution requires context

Automatic captions have no diarization. The introduction names Dwight Collins, co-head of US institutional sales at Autonomous and brother of Porter Collins. Questions, first-person career recollections and extended answers identify speakers. The Upstart exchange has brief ambiguous interjections, reflected in medium attribution confidence.

  • The opening montage repeats later dialogue and is not used as the sole location for claims.
  • Dwight Collins is the guest, not his brother Porter.
  • Automatic captions distort BlackRock, Blackstone and Kovacevich in places.
  • Several anecdotes refer to uncertain historical dates; these are not converted into independently documented contemporary forecasts.
  • The 200-to-50 private-equity example is hypothetical but the asserted accounting rule is substantive.
  • The complete 3,745-second source, including closing remarks and disclaimer, was read.

How he reasons here

  • Distinguish earnings contributors from valuation catalysts.
  • Analyze technology scale and integration costs in bank mergers.
  • Reconcile AUM through flows and market returns.
  • Separate recurring alternative-manager fees from carry and investment income.
  • Check cash realizability and regulatory capital rather than headline insurer earnings.
  • Analyze payment economics by issuer, acquirer and network.
  • Treat governance structure as an investment risk.
